# The two debt tables in the annual town reports — what was read, and what was refused

**Generated by `scripts/extract_debt_tables.py`. Do not edit.**

Two printed tables share the subject `debt` in `annual-report-pages.csv` and are
nothing alike. They are read into two datasets, and neither is published where the
document's own arithmetic does not close on it. The script's docstring carries the
method; this note carries the result.

## FIVE YEARS OUTSTANDING DEBT

`sources/data/outstanding-debt.csv`. Principal outstanding on 30 June, by purpose,
inside and outside the Chapter 44 debt limit.

**Two files here have almost the same name and one of them is dead.**
`sources/data/debt-outstanding.csv` is the earlier attempt at this same table; it is
one line long — a header and no rows — and `scripts/extract_debt_outstanding.py`
still produces nothing, because it looks for the year header in the first eight
lines of a page rendering whose origin is at the BOTTOM left, where the header is in
the last eight. That is a fact about the renderer, not about the reports. Retiring
one of the two names is a decision for a person, not for this script, which is why
both are still on disk.

- **1038 rows**, from **15** annual reports, covering **FY2007 to FY2025**.
- By section: inside the debt limit 415, outside the debt limit 257, printed total 320, short-term 46.

### The headline series, and how many books agree on each year

Each fiscal year is printed by up to five different reports, four years apart, off
the same ledger. This is the check almost nothing else in the archive gets.

| as of 30 June | total long-term indebtedness | reports printing it | agree |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| FY2007 | 29,127,892 | 1 | yes |
| FY2008 | 28,121,418 | 2 | yes |
| FY2009 | 29,490,706 | 3 | yes |
| FY2010 | 29,122,015 | 4 | yes |
| FY2011 | 27,097,992 | 5 | yes |
| FY2012 | 26,479,504 | 4 | yes |
| FY2013 | 24,298,666 | 5 | yes |
| FY2014 | 22,140,230 | 5 | yes |
| FY2015 | 49,556,203 | 5 | yes |
| FY2016 | 52,186,686 | 5 | yes |
| FY2017 | 51,797,859 / 51,797,860 | 5 | NO — see below |
| FY2018 | 49,662,322 | 5 | yes |
| FY2019 | 46,568,549 | 5 | yes |
| FY2020 | 45,109,859 | 5 | yes |
| FY2021 | 41,885,307 | 5 | yes |
| FY2022 | 38,749,085 | 4 | yes |
| FY2023 | 35,563,302 | 3 | yes |
| FY2024 | 33,256,561 | 2 | yes |
| FY2025 | 31,576,807 | 1 | yes |

**FY2017 does not agree.** FY2017 prints 51,797,859; FY2018 prints 51,797,860; FY2019 prints 51,797,860; FY2020 prints 51,797,860; FY2021 prints 51,797,860. One dollar, and this file does not say which book is
right: the difference is below what either scan can settle, and nothing here tests it.

## DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE — the grand totals only

`sources/data/debt-repayment.csv`. What falls due in each FUTURE fiscal year.

- **37 rows**, from **8** reports, for **28** distinct due years.
- Reports represented: FY2011, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, FY2017, FY2019, FY2021, FY2022.

**The per-ISSUE detail is deliberately unread.** It is twenty to twenty-five narrow
columns of small type on a scan, and Apple Vision returns it as runs like
`52782335 52547440 52531098`. No issue-level row can be footed to the printed grand
total in that state, and an unfooted row is not evidence. That is a statement about
the scans, not about the town: the schedule is printed in full in every report.

**A due year is not cross-checkable between reports.** A year of OUTSTANDING debt is
history and two books must agree; a year of future debt SERVICE moves every time the
town issues a bond. Both readings are right.
